name: vscode-idris2
description: Idris 2 language support: the compiler's errors and warnings, types and documentation on hover, go to definition, completion, semantic highlighting, inlay hints, evaluation of expressions, syntax highlighting, editing support, snippets and toolchain detection. Holes and interactive editing are in development.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode the extension runs no program: it does not start idris2, idris2-lsp or pack, not even to read their versions or to check a file, and it reads .ipkg files with a limited built-in reader instead of the compiler. Highlighting, snippets and editing support work as usual. Workspace values of the idris2.toolchain paths and environment and of idris2.ideMode.loosePackages and idris2.ideMode.extraArgs apply only once the workspace is trusted.

idris2.toolchain.idris2Path.markdownDescription: Path to the `idris2` executable. Empty (the default): search `PATH`, then pack's directories (its bin directory, `$PACK_BIN_DIR` or else `~/.local/bin`, then the `bin` directory of pack's current collection under its state directory, if that exists), then on macOS and Linux `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin`, and on every platform `~/.idris2/bin`; with `#idris2.toolchain.preferPack#`, pack's directories come before `PATH`. Only absolute directories are searched (on Windows, ones with a drive or a `\\server\share` root). For pack's directories `~` is the `HOME` of the environment pack's wrappers run with (see `#idris2.toolchain.env#`). When set, only this value is used: an absolute path (on Windows, one with a drive or a `\\server\share` root; one without an extension is tried with the extensions of `PATHEXT`), or a bare command name looked up on `PATH`; if it names nothing, the tool is reported missing and no other place is searched. A leading `~` stands for your home directory. A workspace value applies only in a trusted workspace.

idris2.toolchain.lspPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `idris2-lsp` executable. Empty (the default): searched in the same places as `idris2` (see `#idris2.toolchain.idris2Path#`). When set, only this value is used: an absolute path (on Windows, one with a drive or a `\\server\share` root; one without an extension is tried with the extensions of `PATHEXT`), or a bare command name looked up on `PATH`; if it names nothing, the tool is reported missing and no other place is searched. A leading `~` stands for your home directory. A workspace value applies only in a trusted workspace.

idris2.toolchain.packPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `pack` executable. Empty (the default): searched in the same places as `idris2` (see `#idris2.toolchain.idris2Path#`). The extension never starts pack by itself; it only puts pack commands into a terminal for you to run. (pack's own `idris2` and `idris2-lsp` wrapper scripts call pack whenever they run, including when the extension reads their versions.) When set, only this value is used: an absolute path (on Windows, one with a drive or a `\\server\share` root; one without an extension is tried with the extensions of `PATHEXT`), or a bare command name looked up on `PATH`; if it names nothing, the tool is reported missing and no other place is searched. A leading `~` stands for your home directory. A workspace value applies only in a trusted workspace.

idris2.toolchain.preferPack.markdownDescription: Search pack's directories before `PATH` (see `#idris2.toolchain.idris2Path#`), so that `idris2` and `idris2-lsp` come from the same pack collection even when another `idris2` is first on `PATH`.

idris2.toolchain.env.markdownDescription: Environment variables for the `idris2`, `idris2-lsp` and `pack` processes the extension starts, for example `{ "IDRIS2_PREFIX": "/opt/idris2" }`. Each entry replaces the inherited variable of the same name; values are used as written, without `~` or variable expansion. The search for the executables reads `PATH` (and `PATHEXT` on Windows) and pack's `HOME`, `XDG_*` and `PACK_*` directory variables from this environment too. A workspace value applies only in a trusted workspace.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Check a file when it is opened and each time it is saved.
As `onSave`, and also save an Idris file with unsaved changes once `#idris2.checking.delay#` milliseconds have passed without an edit.
Check a file only with **Idris 2: Check File**.
idris2.checking.trigger.markdownDescription: When the compiler checks an Idris file and reports its errors and warnings. `onSave` (the default): when the file is opened and each time it is saved. `afterDelay`: as `onSave`, and in addition an Idris file with unsaved changes is saved automatically once `#idris2.checking.delay#` milliseconds have passed without an edit — this writes your files. `manual`: only **Idris 2: Check File** checks a file. The compiler always checks the file as saved on disk, not the unsaved text in the editor.

idris2.checking.delay.markdownDescription: Milliseconds without an edit after which an Idris file with unsaved changes is saved when `#idris2.checking.trigger#` is `afterDelay`. From 100 to 2147483647 (about 24.8 days).

markdownEnumDescriptions: Start `idris2 --ide-mode` and use its standard input and output. Nothing listens on a network port.

Start `idris2 --ide-mode-socket` and connect to the local port it prints. The compiler serves the first program that connects to that port, without checking which one: another program on this computer that connects first can use the compiler as you, including running programs.
idris2.ideMode.transport.markdownDescription: How the extension talks to the compiler's IDE mode. `stdio` (the default, on every platform) starts `idris2 --ide-mode` and uses its standard input and output; nothing listens on a port. `socket` starts `idris2 --ide-mode-socket` and connects to the port it prints on `127.0.0.1`: the compiler serves the **first** connection to that port, from any program on this computer and without checking which one, so another program that connects before the extension can use the compiler as you, including running programs. The extension notices when its own connection gets no answer, stops that compiler and does not restart it by itself, but by then the other program may have acted. `socket` was tried on macOS only. This setting is read from your user settings only — not from a workspace's, nor from a remote machine's (such as those a dev container's configuration fills) —, so nothing but your own choice opens the socket. Changing it restarts the running IDE-mode processes.

idris2.ideMode.isolateBuildDir.markdownDescription: Keep the build files (TTC) the compiler writes for the editor in `build/.vscode-idris2` next to the package's `.ipkg` (for a file without a package, next to the file), apart from those of your own `idris2 --build` or `pack build`, by passing `--build-dir`. When the `.ipkg` sets `builddir`, or a `--build-dir` in `opts`, the compiler uses that directory whatever `--build-dir` says, so the editor and your builds share it (and no `--build-dir` is passed); **Idris 2: Stop Backend** stops the editor's compiler before a build. A `--build-dir` in `#idris2.ideMode.extraArgs#` is used instead of this one. The process of **Idris 2: Evaluate Selection** keeps its build files in `build/.vscode-idris2-eval`, whatever this setting says, unless the `.ipkg` or `extraArgs` choose the build directory as above. Changing it restarts the running IDE-mode processes whose command line it changes.

idris2.ideMode.loosePackages.markdownDescription: Installed packages to make available to Idris files that belong to no package (no `.ipkg` in their folder or above it), each passed to the compiler as `-p <name>`: for example `["contrib"]` for a file that imports `Data.String.Extra`. Files in a package get the `depends` of their `.ipkg` instead. A workspace value applies only in a trusted workspace. Changing it restarts the running IDE-mode processes whose command line it changes.

idris2.ideMode.extraArgs.markdownDescription: Additional command-line arguments for every `idris2` IDE-mode process, placed after the extension's own (`--ide-mode` or `--ide-mode-socket`, `--no-color`, `-p`, `--build-dir`) and passed as they are, without a shell. It must not contain `--ide-mode` or `--ide-mode-socket`: the transport is chosen by `#idris2.ideMode.transport#`, in user settings only, and with either of them no IDE-mode process is started (the status says why). A workspace value applies only in a trusted workspace. Changing it restarts the running IDE-mode processes whose command line it changes.

idris2.ideMode.requestTimeout.markdownDescription: Milliseconds the compiler has to answer a quick request, such as the type of a name. IDE mode cannot cancel a request, so one that takes longer stops the compiler's process, and the extension starts a new one. From 1000 to 2147483647 (about 24.8 days).

idris2.ideMode.longActionTimeout.markdownDescription: Milliseconds the compiler has to check a file, search for a proof or generate a definition. IDE mode cannot cancel a request, so one that takes longer stops the compiler's process, and the extension starts a new one. From 1000 to 2147483647 (about 24.8 days).

idris2.ideMode.idleTimeout.markdownDescription: Milliseconds after which an IDE-mode process that has had no request is stopped, to free its memory; it starts again when it is needed. The process of **Idris 2: Evaluate Selection** stops after at most 2 minutes without an evaluation (never when this setting is `0`), and after an evaluation that took more than a second. `0`: never stopped for being idle. At most 2147483647 (about 24.8 days).

idris2.ideMode.maxSessions.markdownDescription: The most IDE-mode compiler processes that keep running at once in this VS Code window; `0` (the default): no limit. Each window counts its own, so with two windows open up to twice as many can run. Each project (each `.ipkg` folder, and each folder of files without one) has its own process, and a second one once you evaluate an expression there (**Idris 2: Evaluate Selection**); both count. Above the limit, idle processes are stopped — never one that is busy: first the evaluation processes, the one used least recently first, then the checking processes of projects other than the active editor's file's, likewise; a stopped process starts again when it is next needed, and then loads its modules again. On a machine with little memory, try `3`. Changing it restarts nothing.

idris2.ideMode.maxBackgroundChecks.markdownDescription: The most checks of files other than the active editor's that run at once in this VS Code window (each window counts its own); `0` (the default): no limit. The others wait and run in the order they were asked for; the active editor's file is checked at once and never waits for them, and a waiting file that becomes the active one is checked at once. A file whose folder waits for your permission to start the compiler takes no turn meanwhile, and **Idris 2: Stop Backend** drops the checks still waiting. Within one project the compiler answers one request at a time: the active file's check goes before the project's other checks that wait, after the one it is working on. On a machine with little memory, try `1`. Changing it restarts nothing.

idris2.diagnostics.includeSourceExcerpt.markdownDescription: Keep the source excerpt the compiler prints under the location of an error or warning in the message shown in the editor and the Problems panel. Off by default, since the editor marks the location itself.

idris2.inlayHints.variableTypes.markdownDescription: Show the type of each pattern variable after it, as the compiler infers it: `: Vect ?_ ?_` after `xs` in `vlen xs = ?vlen_rhs`. The types come from the compiler's last check of the saved file; while the file has unsaved changes the hints of that check stay with their variables. VS Code's `editor.inlayHints.enabled` also applies.

idris2.eval.inlineResults.markdownDescription: Show the result of **Idris 2: Evaluate Selection** in the editor, after the last line of the evaluated text, and in a hover over that text; **Idris 2: Clear Evaluation Results** removes them. Off: the result is shown in a notification instead. Evaluate evaluates expressions only, in a second compiler process of the file's project that starts at the first evaluation: an `IO` action is shown as a value, not run, and REPL commands such as `:exec` are refused.

idris2.eval.timeout.markdownDescription: Milliseconds the compiler has to evaluate an expression for **Idris 2: Evaluate Selection**. IDE mode cannot cancel an evaluation, so one that takes longer stops the evaluation's compiler process, which starts again at the next evaluation; an evaluation that does not end can take more than a gigabyte of memory within seconds. An evaluation still running after a second can also be cancelled from its notification. From 1000 to 2147483647 (about 24.8 days).

markdownEnumDescriptions: `chords` on macOS, `prefix` on Linux and Windows.

`Ctrl+C` followed by `Ctrl+<letter>`, in the style of Emacs and Agda (on macOS the Control key, not Command). On Linux and Windows, `Ctrl+C` then starts a shortcut in Idris editors and no longer copies there.
`Ctrl+Alt+I` followed by the letter. On Linux and Windows, `Ctrl+Alt+I` then starts a shortcut in Idris editors and no longer opens the Chat view there.
No keyboard shortcuts; the commands stay in the Command Palette.
idris2.keybindings.scheme.markdownDescription: Keyboard shortcuts of the Idris 2 commands in Idris editors: the letter `t` runs **Idris 2: Type at Cursor**, `d` **Docs at Cursor** and `e` **Evaluate Selection**. `auto` (the default): `chords` on macOS, `prefix` on Linux and Windows. `chords`: `Ctrl+C` followed by `Ctrl+<letter>`, e.g. `Ctrl+C Ctrl+T` (on macOS the Control key); on Linux and Windows `Ctrl+C` then no longer copies in Idris editors. `prefix`: `Ctrl+Alt+I` followed by the letter, e.g. `Ctrl+Alt+I T`; on Linux and Windows `Ctrl+Alt+I` then no longer opens the Chat view in Idris editors. `none`: no shortcuts. A keymap extension that binds `Ctrl+C` itself (VSCodeVim does in its default configuration) takes precedence over `chords`: choose `prefix` then. Read from your user settings only: a workspace cannot change your keyboard.

idris2.trace.protocol.markdownDescription: Record every message exchanged with the compiler's IDE mode in the output channel "Idris 2: Protocol Trace" (**Idris 2: Show Protocol Trace**), and enable **Idris 2 (Developer): Send Raw Protocol Request…**. For diagnosing problems: the trace contains your source text and file paths, and stays on this machine. User settings only: neither a workspace nor a remote machine's settings can turn it on.

semanticTokenTypes.description: An escape hatch such as believe_me or assert_total (Idris 2 decoration `postulate`).

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Idris 2
walkthroughs.description: Find the Idris 2 toolchain, install what is missing, and open a project.

steps.title: Find the Idris 2 toolchain
steps.description:
The extension looks for `idris2`, `idris2-lsp` and `pack` on this machine. Setup Information shows what it found and where.
[Show Setup Information](command:idris2.showSetupInformation)

steps.title: Install what is missing
steps.description:
The extension installs nothing by itself: each command opens a terminal with the install command typed in for you to review and run, or opens the installation instructions.
[Install Idris 2…](command:idris2.installIdris2)
[Install pack…](command:idris2.installPack)
[Install or Update idris2-lsp with pack](command:idris2.installIdris2Lsp)

steps.title: Open an Idris 2 project
steps.description:
Open the folder of your package (the directory with its `.ipkg` file), or any folder of `.idr` files.
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.mjs --production
scripts.compile: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.mjs
scripts.pretest: npm run compile-tests && npm run compile
scripts.test:e2e: npm run compile-tests && npm run compile && vscode-test --label e2e
scripts.test:corpus: node scripts/fetch-corpus.mjs && npm run compile-tests && mocha --ui tdd out/test/grammar/corpus.test.js
